book.title: Ahmed Yesevî: A Wise Teacher and His Student (A1)

pages.title: A Great Teacher
pages.content:
Ahmed Yesevî was a great Turkish poet and teacher. He was the first great Sufi poet in the Turkish language. Sufis want to be very close to Allah. They live a simple life and remember Allah all the time.

Ahmed Yesevî’s poems have a special name: “hikmet”. This word means “wisdom”. He also had a school. There, he taught Islam to the Turkish people in Turkestan. The Turkish people were learning the rules of Islam in their own language. They spoke Turkish. People call him “Pîr-i Turkistan”. It means “the guide of Turkestan”.

vocabulary.definition: A person who writes poems.
A Muslim who wants to be very close to Allah.
A short text with lines, like a song.
Knowing the right and good way.
A person who shows you the way.

pages.title: Young Ahmed
pages.content:
Ahmed was born in East Turkestan more than 900 years ago. When he was young, he went to the city of Yesi. Today, Yesi is in Kazakhstan. There, he studied with a wise teacher, Arslan Baba.

Later, he went to Bukhara, a big city of Islam and science. Today, Bukhara is in Uzbekistan. Ahmed learned from great teachers there. Then he returned to Yesi. He taught people there until he died in 1166.

pages.title: Easy Words
pages.content:
Ahmed Yesevî talked to people in simple Turkish. Everybody understood him, and people loved him. They came to him from many different places.

His poems tell us about wisdom. But what is wisdom? Every day, we do many things. Rules tell us “What do I do?” and “How do I do it?” Wisdom answers a different question: “Why do I do it?” When we know the answer, our work has a real meaning.

vocabulary.definition: Words that tell us the right thing to do.
The reason for something; why it is important.

pages.title: A Boy with the Qur’an
pages.content:
One day, Ahmed Yesevî was in front of his school. Some children walked past on their way to the mosque for Qur’an lessons. Most of them carried their Qur’ans in bags. But one boy carried his Qur’an on his head. He showed respect to the Qur’an, and Ahmed Yesevî smiled.

After the lesson, the boy walked past the school again. This time, he walked backwards. He did not want to turn his back to his teacher. Ahmed Yesevî was very pleased with the little boy’s respect. Ahmed Yesevî said to him, “My son, ask your mother and father. Then come to my lessons.” The boy’s family said yes. The boy’s name was Süleyman.

pages.title: Wood in the Rain
pages.content:
Süleyman started to learn from Ahmed Yesevî. One day, Ahmed Yesevî sent Süleyman and his friends out for wood. The school kitchen needed it. The students collected the wood. But on the way back, it started to rain.

Süleyman thought, “We cannot cook with wet wood.” So he took off his coat and put it around his wood. Back at the school, the other children’s wood was wet. It did not burn. But Süleyman’s wood was dry, and it burned well. Ahmed Yesevî said, “My son, you have a wise heart. Your name is Hakîm Süleyman now.” Hakîm means “wise”.

vocabulary.definition: The hard part of a tree.

pages.title: Hakîm Ata
pages.content:
Süleyman learned a lot of lessons from his teacher. They were very useful and important. He grew up at his school. Later, people called him Hakîm Ata.

After many years, Hakîm Ata went to Khwarazm. Today, this place is in Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. He taught Islam and good manners to the people there. He was an early teacher for the Turkish people. Like his teacher Ahmed Yesevî, he also wrote poems in Turkish.

vocabulary.definition: The polite way to do things.

pages.title: Wise Words
pages.content:
Hakîm Ata has some famous words. One of them is about guests and nights: “See every guest as Khizr, and see every night as Laylat al-Qadr.” In Turkish, it is “Her geleni Hızır, her geceyi Kadir bil.” Khizr is a good and wise servant of Allah. Laylat al-Qadr is a very special night in Ramadan.

Turkish people still use these words today.

exercises.instructions: Put each verb in the right group.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 3: “Everybody understood him, and people loved him.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the first paragraph of Chapter 3.

exercises.title: Who Is It?
exercises.instructions: Match the person with the sentence.
exercises.question: Who is it?

matchingPairs.right: He was young Ahmed’s wise teacher.
He put his coat around his wood.

correctAnswer.Arslan Baba: He was young Ahmed’s wise teacher.
correctAnswer.Süleyman: He put his coat around his wood.

exercises.explanation: Chapter 2: Arslan Baba. Chapter 5: Süleyman. Chapter 6: Hakîm Ata.

feedback.incorrect: Read Chapters 2, 5 and 6 again.

exercises.title: Backwards
exercises.question: Why did the boy walk backwards?
options: He did not want to turn his back to his teacher.
He was afraid of the rain.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 4: “He did not want to turn his back to his teacher.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 4.

exercises.title: The Wood
exercises.question: Süleyman’s wood was wet.
exercises.explanation: Chapter 5: “But Süleyman’s wood was dry, and it burned well.”

feedback.correct: Yes, it is false. His wood was dry.
feedback.incorrect: Read the second paragraph of Chapter 5.

exercises.title: Wise Words
exercises.question: Do Turkish people use Hakîm Ata’s words today?
exercises.explanation: Chapter 7: “Turkish people still use these words today.”

feedback.incorrect: Read the last sentence of Chapter 7.

exercises.title: The Teacher and His Student
exercises.question: What happened first?

sequencingItems.text: Ahmed Yesevî studied in Yesi and Bukhara.
Ahmed Yesevî saw a boy with the Qur’an on his head.
Ahmed Yesevî gave Süleyman a new name: Hakîm Süleyman.

exercises.explanation: Yesi and Bukhara (Chapter 2) → the boy (Chapter 4) → a new name (Chapter 5) → Khwarazm (Chapter 6).

feedback.correct: Great! You know the story of the teacher and his student.
feedback.incorrect: Think about the order of the chapters.
